pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 4.5.1 NARRATIVE AND DESCRIPTIVE PARAGRAPHS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.5: Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we make a narrative composition interesting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write narrative and descriptive paragraphs
2. use the first person and second person in narrative and descriptive paragraphs
3. value the need for well formed paragraphs in written communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 4.5.1 NARRATIVE AND DESCRIPTIVE PARAGRAPHS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 4.5.1 NARRATIVE AND DESCRIPTIVE PARAGRAPHS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write narrative and descriptive paragraphs

What this means
In this part you learn to write narrative and descriptive paragraphs. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write narrative and descriptive paragraphs.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write narrative and descriptive paragraphs. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use the first person and second person in narrative and descriptive paragraphs

What this means
In this part you learn to use the first person and second person in narrative and descriptive paragraphs. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the first person and second person in narrative and descriptive paragraphs.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the first person and second person in narrative and descriptive paragraphs. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value the need for well formed paragraphs in written communication

What this means
In this part you learn to value the need for well formed paragraphs in written communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the need for well formed paragraphs in written communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the need for well formed paragraphs in written communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write narrative and descriptive paragraphs)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs to a partner. (skill: use the first person and second person in narrative and descriptive paragraphs)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: value the need for well formed paragraphs in written communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write narrative and descriptive paragraphs.
3. Practise this skill: use the first person and second person in narrative and descriptive paragraphs.
4. Practise this skill: value the need for well formed paragraphs in written communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we make a narrative composition interesting?
2. How can we ensure unity in a paragraph?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 4.5.1 Narrative and Descriptive Paragraphs means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write narrative and descriptive paragraphs.
5. Be able to: use the first person and second person in narrative and descriptive paragraphs.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
